items.title: STAREE: statins cut major cardiovascular events 30% in healthy over-70s — but not disability-free survival
items.summary: Presented in a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026 in Munich and published simultaneously in the New England Journal of Medicine, STAREE randomised 9,971 Australians aged 70+ with no known cardiovascular disease, diabetes or dementia to atorvastatin 40 mg daily or placebo. Over a median 5.9 years, major cardiovascular events fell 30% (6.0% vs 8.3%; HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.61–0.82). The co-primary endpoint of disability-free survival was not significantly improved (12.8% vs 13.6%; HR 0.94, p=0.25).
items.why: The first large primary-prevention statin trial in over-70s gives Protocol hard evidence to act on lipid findings in older screening clients — while the null disability endpoint is a caution against overselling healthspan claims.

items.title: CMS says it has blocked $1.6bn in improper Medicare lab payments, revoking 157 laboratories
items.summary: CMS announced it has prevented more than $1.6 billion in potentially fraudulent Medicare laboratory payments, including revoking 157 laboratory providers (approximately $732 million in savings) and suspending over $500 million in payments tied to investigations of hundreds of labs. The agency says AI and machine-learning analytics were used to flag unusual billing patterns. All figures are as reported by CMS and should be treated as approximate.
items.why: Payer and regulator scrutiny of high-volume lab billing is intensifying; cash-pay, transparent-price screening models like Protocol's largely sidestep this risk, but expect harder questions everywhere on justifying broad test panels.

items.title: FDA clears Roche Elecsys pTau217 — first single-biomarker blood test to both rule in and rule out Alzheimer's amyloid
items.summary: Roche announced FDA clearance of Elecsys Phospho-Tau (217P) Plasma, developed with Eli Lilly, to aid identification of amyloid pathology in people aged 55+ with signs or symptoms of cognitive decline. Roche describes it as the first FDA-cleared single-biomarker blood test supporting both rule-in and rule-out assessment using the same validated cutoffs across primary and specialty care. Press reports describe it as the fourth Alzheimer's blood test cleared by the FDA in under two years.
items.why: Neuro-cognitive biomarkers are moving out of specialist referral and into ordinary blood panels — a credible future pillar alongside Protocol's metabolic, hormonal and cancer screening, though the clearance covers symptomatic patients, not asymptomatic screening.

items.title: FDA authorises the first wearable that continuously monitors both glucose and ketones
items.summary: The FDA granted marketing authorisation to the Libre Duo 10 Day Continuous Dual Glucose Ketone Monitoring System for people aged 2 and older living with diabetes. The sensor measures both ketones and glucose in interstitial fluid every minute and can alert users when ketone levels approach a concerning threshold, ahead of diabetic ketoacidosis. FDA says the clinical programme drew on six studies enrolling more than 600 participants (approximate — verify against the FDA release).
items.why: Continuous metabolic sensing keeps widening beyond glucose; ketone data pairs naturally with GLP-1 and weight-loss coaching and raises the bar for what counts as metabolic monitoring in an integrated longevity programme.
